chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “If the insane person or the mentally deficient person commits zina, the hadd is administered by flogging, and if he is muḥṣan, he is stoned.”
I said: “What is the difference between the insane man and the insane woman, and the mentally deficient man and the mentally deficient woman?”

He said: “The woman is only approached, while the man approaches; and he only approaches when he understands how he comes to the pleasure. As for the woman, she may only be compelled and the act done to her while she does not understand what is being done to her.”

key_terms.الْمَجْنُونُ: the insane man; one described as lacking sound reason
key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهُ: the mentally deficient man; one with impaired understanding
key_terms.جُلِدَ الْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment of flogging was carried out
key_terms.رُجِمَ: he was stoned as the prescribed hadd punishment
key_terms.لَا تَعْقِلُ: she does not comprehend or understand
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through iḥṣān, implying a status relevant to the hadd of zina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zina involving an insane or mentally deficient person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning zina committed by a mentally impaired male and then clarifies a distinction between male and female cases. It explains the distinction in terms of agency and comprehension in the act, framing the ruling within a jurisprudential discussion of legal responsibility.
